title: Hosted API plugin slimline handshake and checkpointing — PRD (rough)
content:
Context / problem statement:

We keep seeing two correlated engineering asks from customers and SDK teams: (1) low-bandwidth or intermittent clients (mobile, edge workers, offline-first webviews) need predictable, resumable, and tiny-footprint streaming interactions with Hosted API; (2) customers want safe, lightweight tool/plugin integrations (toollets) that can be provisioned and run with minimal per-call overhead and clear lifecycle semantics.

Existing hosted streaming work focuses on large, long-lived sessions and typed streaming contracts. That model is heavyweight for short-lived plugin calls from constrained clients. Meanwhile, clients resort to ad-hoc polling, ad-hoc local proxies, or expensive always-on socket connections. We should provide a first-class pattern for: 
- a compact handshake for ephemeral plugin/tool sessions,
- checkpointed incremental output (token-aligned) that can be resumed after network blips,
- a lease/expiry model for plugin resources (so hosted runtime can evict cleanly), and
- SDK ergonomics (small client code, polyglot) so it’s low friction to adopt.

Goal (what success looks like):
- Reduce median bytes-on-wire for a plugin handshake by >= 3x vs current streaming handshake.
- Allow client resume-once semantics for partially streamed responses (resume within TTL) with end-to-end correctness in 95% of transient-failure cases.
- Introduce a simple plugin lease model with explicit lifecycle APIs (acquire, heartbeat, release) and server-side eviction policy documented.
- Deliver SDK surfaces (Go, Python, TypeScript, Swift/Kotlin sample wrappers) with < 100 lines of glue code for typical call patterns.
- Beta with 3 external customers in Q2 2025 and internal SDK adoption in 6 weeks.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not attempt to replace the full-fidelity typed-streaming API; it's a complementary surface for short plugin calls and intermittent clients.
- Not addressing multi-tenant GPU scheduling or placement-optimizations beyond coarse policy hints.

User stories / example flows:
1) Mobile note-taking app: user triggers a short plugin that extracts action items from a selection. Client opens a tiny handshake socket (or HTTP/2 stream), sends plugin-id + short context, receives incremental tokens and a final commit frame. If network drops, the app reconnects with the last received token index and resumes.

2) Edge webhook processor: serverless worker obtains a plugin lease, runs a short deterministic tool (e.g., reranker), then releases the lease. Leasing ensures predictable billing and resource reclamation.

3) Web embed with offline cache: page can request a partial summary, cache the checkpointed state and later rehydrate by resuming the session or replaying the checkpoint locally.

Key concepts / primitives:
- Compact Handshake: minimal proto that sends (client_id, plugin_id, auth_token, optional proto-hint) in <= 512 bytes. Negotiation answers with a session_id and capabilities bitmask. Avoid sending model description & heavy telemetry in the handshake; move those to async telemetry channels.

- Token-Indexed Checkpoints: streaming responses include lightweight checkpoint markers (token_index, checkpoint_id, optional compressed prefix digest). Checkpoint frames are idempotent and small (<< 1KB).

- Resume Protocol: clients reconnect and provide (session_id | checkpoint_id, last_token_index_received, client_nonce). Server validates and resumes streaming from next token. Resume is best-effort but returns a clear reconciliation header if content divergence detected (e.g., model restarted with different seed), allowing client fallbacks.

- Plugin Lease Semantics: leases with TTL (default 30s for ephemeral calls, configurable up to 5m for longer tasks). Acquire returns session_id + lease_expiry. Heartbeat endpoint to extend lease. On expiry, server marks plugin resources reclaimable and emits eviction event. Leases are soft: final commit frames may still be accepted for a short grace.

- Small-footprint SDK Surface: single small module per language exposing: acquirePlugin(), callPluginStream(), resumeStream(), releasePlugin(), with promise/async iterator ergonomics for incremental tokens and a small sync fallback.

API sketches (very rough):
- POST /v1/plugins/acquire -> {session_id, lease_expires_at}
- POST /v1/plugins/{session_id}/stream (chunked/streaming response with frames)
- POST /v1/plugins/{session_id}/resume -> {resume_ok: true/false, reconcile_hint?}
- POST /v1/plugins/{session_id}/heartbeat -> {lease_expires_at}
- POST /v1/plugins/{session_id}/release -> {released: true}

Streaming frame types (compact):
- FRAME:tokens {start_index:int, data: base64-or-text, is_final:bool}
- FRAME:checkpoint {checkpoint_id:uuid, prev_end_index:int, digest:hex}
- FRAME:meta {reconcile_hint:short-string}
- FRAME:commit {status: ok|error, tool_outcome_id}

SDK ergonomics notes (guiding constraints):
- Keep dependency count minimal; shipping a ~20KB JS wrapper for web use is our target.
- Provide single-file Swift/Kotlin examples for in-app use.
- Expose incremental iterator that emits both tokens and checkpoint events so apps can persist checkpoints easily.
- Transparent fallbacks: if client cannot do streaming, provide single-response compile that returns compressed checkpoints.

Safety, security, rate limits:
- Plugin acquisition should surface role-based constraints (customer may restrict which plugins are available to certain API keys).
- Checkpoint frames do not contain secret material; prevent accidental leakage by stripping any KMS/HSM references.
- Rate limit: per-API-key concurrent plugin leases limited by plan (e.g., starter 3, standard 50, enterprise custom).

Operational considerations / server behavior:
- Eviction window: server marks lease expired at t0, allows short grace to accept final commit if within grace window. Grace defaults to 10s; configurable per customer tier.
- Metrics to add: lease_acquire_rate, lease_eviction_rate, resume_success_rate, avg_bytes_per_handshake, median_resume_latency, percent_sessions_with_checkpoint.

Failure modes and reconciliation strategies:
- Divergence on resume: detect via prefix digest mismatch, return reconcile_hint and optionally snapshot-of-latest-final-output for client to reconcile (size-capped).
- Lost final commit due to eviction: best-effort commit retry recommended; client should persist checkpoint locally before lease expiry.

Open questions / trade-offs (to resolve in implementation sprint):
- Should handshake be purely HTTP/2/3 or allow an authenticated WebSocket path? (WebSocket simplifies incremental delivery for some mobile runtimes.)
- Binary vs text checkpoints: base64-on-wire is simplest compatibility; but binary frames (CBOR) are smaller. Trade-off: SDK weight vs perf.
- Default lease TTL & grace windows per plan — what are sensible defaults?
- How to expose replayability / local simulation hooks for SDKs (helpful for dev testing).

Implementation roadmap (candidate milestones):
- M1 (2 weeks): spec sign-off, API prototype (POST-based streaming + checkpoint frames), JS + Python minimal wrappers. Internal dogfood.
- M2 (4 weeks): resume semantics, heartbeat API, sample Swift/Kotlin wrappers, instrumentation, logging.
- M3 (6 weeks): rate-limits by plan, eviction grace tuning, telemetry dashboards. Begin external beta.
- M4 (8 weeks): customer feedback loop, iterate on handshake compactness and add WebSocket option if needed.

Success metrics (first 12 weeks):
- SDK adoption: 4 internal teams adopt plugin-slimline API into prototypes.
- Resume success: >= 90% resume_success_rate in controlled flaky-network tests.
- Bandwidth: median handshake payload < 700 bytes in standard case.
- Latency: median time-to-first-token <= 180ms for regional requests.

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- Product + Eng sync to pick binary vs text framing (Mar 3). Marcus to own prototyping.
- Security to approve lease-eviction telemetry payload shape (Mar 7).
- Draft SDK public examples (TS, Python) and add to developer quickstart (Mar 14).
- Sales / Solutions to onboard 2 pilot customers for beta by Apr 1.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally rough; aim is to get alignment on primitives (handshake, checkpoint, lease) rather than final wire format.
- When commenting: mark whether comment is "spec", "sdk", or "ops" to help triage.

Small appendix: quick UX note for app developers
- Minimal pattern: acquire -> callStream (subscribe tokens+checkpoints) -> persist checkpoint on checkpoint event -> release (or auto-release after success).
- Fallback pattern: if resume fails, fetch final committed output via a single non-streaming GET with session_id fallback.

End of doc (rough) — this should be treated as a high-level product-protocol sketch.
